GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

All five options are AI-generated - do not consider the possibility that a human wrote it. Read the text carefully and identify which model most likely produced it, based on writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- TEXT ---
In the digital age, the pervasive nature of social media often compromises our psychological health, but consciously reducing the time spent on these platforms can significantly enhance overall wellbeing. One of the most immediate benefits of limiting social media use is the mitigation of constant social comparison. Online platforms are designed as curated galleries where individuals showcase only their most successful, attractive, and exciting moments. When users spend hours scrolling through these idealized depictions of life, they inevitably compare their own daily struggles and mundane routines to the highlight reels of others. This disparity breeds feelings of inadequacy, envy, and anxiety. By stepping back from the digital spotlight, individuals can break this toxic cycle of comparison, fostering a healthier self-image and learning to appreciate their own lives based on personal values rather than superficial online standards.

Beyond emotional relief, minimizing social media consumption directly frees up a substantial amount of time that can be redirected toward more fulfilling offline activities. The addictive design of modern applications, characterized by infinite scrolls and push notifications, quietly robs people of hours each day. Reclaiming this lost time allows individuals to engage in tangible experiences that promote genuine personal growth and happiness. Instead of passively consuming content, people can invest their energy into reading, physical exercise, exploring creative hobbies, or fostering face-to-face relationships. These real-world activities provide a sense of tangible accomplishment, deep connection, and mindfulness that virtual interactions simply cannot replicate, ultimately leading to a more purposeful and satisfying life.

Finally, reducing social media use, particularly during the evening hours, dramatically improves sleep quality by limiting exposure to electronic screens. The blue light emitted by smartphones and tablets interferes with the body’s natural circadian rhythm by suppressing the production of melatonin, the hormone responsible for regulating sleep. Furthermore, the psychologically stimulating and often stressful nature of social media content keeps the brain highly alert, making it difficult to transition into a restful state. By establishing boundaries around screen time and putting devices away before bed, individuals allow their minds to unwind naturally. This practice leads to quicker sleep onset and deeper, more restorative rest, which in turn boosts daytime mood, cognitive function, and physical health, proving that a break from the virtual world is essential for holistic wellbeing.
--- END ---
Output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
